subject: MAP: PoC acceptance gates, geofence & deployment-mode decision
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira@novushealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff — PoC acceptance gates and geofence constraints

Grace / team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal & security folks want a clear mutual action plan (MAP) so we can sign off on the PoC and decide on hosting mode and region. High-level asks from regulatory: EU data residency for PHI, encryption-at-rest + key control options, and SOC2 artifacts. From engineering: latency targets for patient workflows (p95 < 250ms for inference), and an ops fall-back plan if capacity spikes.

Could you send a draft MAP with:
- PoC acceptance gates (functional + perf + security)
- A proposed timeline to decision (we need a firm go/no-go by Aug 25)
- Recommended default deployment (hosted vs dedicated vs private) per risk-profile and a short rationale

Attaching a short list of regulatory questions — we can add procurement and legal once the MAP is stable.

Best,
Samira Patel
Director, Integrations — Novus Health

Attachment: Regulatory_questions.docx (word doc, 12KB)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira@novushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — PoC acceptance gates and geofence constraints

Samira — thanks, this is exactly the right place to start. I put together an initial MAP and a short evidence pack (SOC2 summary) for your regulatory team. Key points up front:

- PoC scope: 2-week integration with sample EHR flows, automated regression set of 250 prompts, and perf windowed tests (cold/steady-state).
- Acceptance gates: functional correctness (>= 95% intents), perf p95 < 250ms (in-hosted baseline), security checklist passed (SOC2 + encryption-at-rest + KMS options documented).
- Timeline: PoC week 1 (integration + smoke tests) -> week 2 (stress + acceptance). Target decision by 2026-08-25.
- Deployment recs: propose Hosted API for PoC to minimize friction and get telemetry quickly; recommend Dedicated reserved capacity for production if you commit to a throughput profile (predictable cost/SLA). Private (VPC/on-prem) is available if Novus requires customer-managed keys or air-gapped requirements — that increases lead time (4–8 weeks) and ops cost.

I've attached Novus_MAP_v1.xlsx (draft milestones) and SOC2_evidence_summary.pdf. Karthik — flagged a couple technical notes inline (latency/caching trade-offs). Marissa — I captured commercial milestones on the MAP tab; can you add the renewal/credit language once we lock a commit?

Propose a 30-minute alignment call Monday or Tuesday next week to lock the timeline.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Novus_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB); SOC2_evidence_summary.pdf (pdf, 95KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira@novushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — PoC acceptance gates and geofence constraints

Looping in a quick tech note so Novus can plan acceptance tests and infra expectations. Replying inline to Grace's bullets: 

- Hosted PoC baseline: our hosted clusters will give lowest onboarding friction. For p95 under 250ms we rely on prefix caching + request batching thresholds. For small request volumes hosted will meet targets in steady-state; cold starts (first tokens) can spike but are rare with continuous warmers.

- Dedicated for production: provides reserved GPU pools, predictable latency SLOs (we can commit to a p95 latency SLO in an SLR with appropriate commit levels). Cost estimate delta: hosted per-token run-rate vs dedicated reserved (attempt): hosted ~ $0.012/token; dedicated (committed) ~ $0.007/token at 1M tokens/day profile. Exact numbers depend on sequence length and batching.

- Private (VPC or on-prem): required if Novus must control keys (HSM/KMS) or stay air-gapped. Expect provisioning lead time 4–8 weeks for VPC/private deployment plus network/peering work. Operationally we recommend an initial hosted PoC, then a staged dedicated commit or private cutover depending on regulatory signoff.

- Regional/geofence note: we can pin runs to EU regions; if PHI must never leave EU we recommend dedicated or private in an EU region to remove cross-border egress concerns. Hosted can be provisioned in eu-west-1 but the governance paperwork needs to be explicit on data residency in the MAP.

I'll bring perf numbers to the align call.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Samira Patel <samira@novushealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Regulatory Team <regulatory@novushealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@novushealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T10:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — PoC acceptance gates and geofence constraints

Thanks Grace and Karthik — this layout helps. A few follow-ups from Regulatory and Procurement: 

- Regulatory: please send the SOC2 attachments and a short note on encryption key control options (customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed). If hosted in EU, confirm data never leaves EU by design and provide the logging/audit retention for 13 months minimum. Regulatory attached some initial questions (see attached).
- Procurement: what are the procurement steps if we choose Dedicated committed capacity vs Hosted pay-as-you-go? Lead times and sample MSA/Exhibit would be helpful.

Can we do a 30-min call Tuesday 2026-08-12 at 14:00 CEST (that's 05:00 PDT) — alternatively Tue 16:00 CEST / 07:00 PDT. We prefer Tue afternoon CEST.

If we opt for Hosted for the PoC but plan a Dedicated commit for production, Procurement would like a draft statement of work and a commitment cadence in the MAP (so legal can budget).

Regards,
Samira Patel
Director, Integrations — Novus Health

Attachment: Regulatory_questions.docx (updated, 9KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — PoC acceptance gates and geofence constraints

Samira — appreciate the clarity. I updated the MAP with a milestone table (MAP_vfinal.xlsx) and a draft commercial cadence:

- PoC start: 2026-08-16
- Integration complete (smoke): 2026-08-20
- Stress + acceptance: 2026-08-21 to 2026-08-24
- Decision window / Go-no-go: by 2026-08-25

Commercial options we discussed: Hosted PoC (no commit) -> Dedicated commit for production (30 / 60 / 90 day ramp options). As a gesture to shorten procurement cycles, we can offer a 10% first-year TCV credit for a dedicated 12-month commit if Novus signs by Sep 15. I attached the MAP with the commercial tab called "CommitScenarios".

Please confirm the Tue CEST time that works for you and I'll set up a 30-minute meeting invite and share a draft SOW + sample MSA exhibit for the Dedicated option.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
